title: HINT for Learning Design — every objective is assessed
metaDescription: Keep objectives, activities, assessments, rubrics and accessibility rules aligned so assistants create course material without invented facts.
h1: Your assistant creates lessons fast. HINT keeps every objective aligned.
intro: HINT keeps course goals, activities, assessments, rubrics and accessibility rules in plain-text notes beside learning materials. Your assistant reads the design for this course before writing a lesson or assessment.

situations.before: A learning objective cannot be observed or measured.
situations.body: The assistant works from your declared standard and flags vague verbs before they spread into activities.

situations.before: An exam tests content that no objective covers.
situations.body: Every activity and assessment names the objectives it serves, making omissions visible.

situations.before: Rubric levels change meaning from one criterion to another.
situations.body: Declared descriptors and grading policy travel with the rubric while course-specific rules remain scoped.

example.intro: The Greendale Courses demo grounds its Spanish 101 syllabus in SRC-1.
example.after: It builds the course document inside the approved alignment, applies accessibility rules, and marks unsupported facts for a source.
example.compiled:
<course name="spanish-101-1">
  Approved course grounded in SRC-1.
</course>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: Invent a fact in course content without a cited material.
Assess an objective that the course never declared.
Change grading policy outside the approved grading rules.
disclaimer: HINT supports course design documentation; instructors and institutions remain responsible for academic accuracy, accessibility and approval.

faq.q: Does it export to an LMS?
faq.a: HINT works with Markdown artifacts; connect the generated material to your LMS through its existing import or publishing process.
Only if you declare the verb and objective rules your program uses; HINT does not impose a framework.

faq.q: Can courses use different grading policies?
faq.a: Yes. Put each course's grading rules in its folder so they do not leak into another course.

keywordDescriptions.course: Sets the title, audience, level and duration.
keywordDescriptions.module: Groups ordered objectives, activities and materials.
keywordDescriptions.objective: Defines a measurable learning objective with a stable identifier.
keywordDescriptions.activity: Names what learners do and the objective it supports.
keywordDescriptions.assessment: States how declared objectives are evaluated.
keywordDescriptions.rubric: Groups consistent criteria and performance levels.
keywordDescriptions.criterion: Defines one observable dimension in a rubric.
keywordDescriptions.alignment: Links objectives to activities and assessments.
